statement: Let c0 = image[sr][sc], and let R be the set of cells (i,j) with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n for which there exists a finite sequence (i_0,j_0),...,(i_k,j_k) with k >= 0 such that (i_0,j_0) = (sr,sc), (i_k,j_k) = (i,j), every (i_t,j_t) lies in the grid, image[i_t][j_t] = c0 for every t, and for every t < k the cells (i_t,j_t) and (i_{t+1},j_{t+1}) share a side, i.e. |i_{t+1}-i_t| + |j_{t+1}-j_t| = 1. The function returns a result r such that len(r) = m, every row of r has length n, and for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n: if (i,j) is in R then r[i][j] = color, and if (i,j) is not in R then r[i][j] = image[i][j].
preconditions: Let m = len(image) and n = len(image[0]). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 50, 1 <= n <= 50, every row of image has length n, for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n we have 0 <= image[i][j] < 65536, 0 <= color < 65536, 0 <= sr < m, and 0 <= sc < n.

statement: Whenever flood_fill returns a result r, len(r) = len(image), and for every i with 0 <= i < len(image), len(r[i]) = len(image[i]).
preconditions: Let m = len(image) and n = len(image[0]). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 50, 1 <= n <= 50, every row of image has length n, for every i,j with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n we have 0 <= image[i][j] < 65536, 0 <= color < 65536, 0 <= sr < m, and 0 <= sc < n.

statement: Let c0 = image[sr][sc], and let R be the set of cells reachable from (sr,sc) by a path of side-adjacent cells all of whose image values equal c0, including (sr,sc) itself.
